findings.title: Public group members page only loads first 50 members
findings.body: The route calls model.findMembers(), and Discourse.Group defaults limit to 50. The group members template iterates members and has no pagination controls, so groups with more than 50 members will display an incomplete member list. Previously non-automatic groups loaded all members.

findings.title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative limit/offset
findings.body: limit and offset are taken directly from request parameters without validation. Negative values can generate invalid SQL, limit=0 produces a zero limit in meta, and an arbitrarily large limit can load and serialize every member of a group from a public endpoint. Clamp limit to a sane positive maximum and ensure offset is non-negative.

findings.title: totalPages adds an extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is exactly divisible by limit (for example 50 users with limit 50), this returns 2 instead of 1. That makes showingLast false on the real last page and allows Next to request an empty page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), with special handling for zero users.

findings.title: Admin group route does not reset pagination offset
findings.body: setupController calls model.findMembers() without resetting the group's offset. Admin group models are cached in the adminGroups controller, so a previously selected page offset can persist. Returning to a group may load a later page or an empty page instead of the first page of members. Reset offset before calling findMembers.

findings.title: findMembers clamps offset to user_count instead of the last valid page start
findings.body: findMembers clamps offset with Math.min(user_count, Math.max(offset, 0)). An offset equal to user_count is a page past the end and will return no members. The offset should be clamped to a valid page start, for example Math.max(0, user_count - limit), or otherwise normalized before requesting members.

findings.title: Group creation ignores alias_level sent by the client
findings.body: The admin UI sends alias_level in Group.asJSON when creating a group, but the create action only assigns name and visible. The group is persisted with the default alias_level while the client-side model still holds the selected value, causing the UI and database to disagree until another explicit save occurs. Create should assign alias_level or the client should not send it on create.

findings.title: add_members silently skips invalid usernames
findings.body: add_members splits the usernames string and ignores any token that does not match a user. It also does not strip whitespace around tokens. The endpoint still returns success, so an admin can mistype usernames or paste a malformed list and receive no indication that some or all users were not added. Invalid or skipped usernames should be reported.

findings.title: Breaking change to /groups/:group_id/members response shape
findings.body: The members endpoint previously rendered an array of serialized users, but now returns an object with members and meta. Any external client, plugin, or script consuming the old array response will break. If this endpoint is considered a public or stable API, the change needs compatibility handling or clear versioning/documentation.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses PUT instead of DELETE
findings.body: The route for remove_member is a DELETE route, but the automatic-group test issues xhr :put, :remove_member. This does not exercise the actual route/verb and can mask routing regressions. The test should use xhr :delete.

findings.title: No specs for the new paginated members endpoint
findings.body: The public members action was changed to accept limit/offset and return members plus meta, but there are no controller/request specs covering normal paging, total counts, invalid/negative/huge limit or offset values, or permissions. Add tests for the new response contract and edge cases.

findings.title: add_members assumes usernames parameter is a string
findings.body: params.require(:usernames) is passed directly to split. If a client sends usernames as an array, for example usernames[], split raises NoMethodError and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Validate/coerce the parameter or accept arrays.

findings.title: remove_member treats invalid user_id as 0
findings.body: user_id is coerced with to_i, so non-numeric values become 0. The action may then perform no deletion and still return success. The controller should validate that user_id identifies a real user and that the user is a member before reporting success.

findings.title: Save error handler assumes JSON errors payload
findings.body: The save failure handler does $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors. If the server returns non-JSON, an empty response, or JSON without an errors property, this throws and the user receives no useful error message. Use safer error handling consistent with Discourse's AJAX error conventions.
